articles.title: Security alert as Nvidia boss admits affair with suspected Chinese spy | BBC News
articles.titleZh: 英伟达老板承认与疑似中国间谍有染的安全警报| BBC新闻
articles.summary:
US tech giant Nvidia has begun an investigation following claims its CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.

Nvidia is one of the world's largest companies and is central to making cutting-edge computer chips that power emerging AI technologies. The company said its board had no reason to believe that its secrets or national security had been compromised.

According to the New York Times, US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security. 

Jensen Huang has admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He said he "full responsibility" for what he did and had fallen short of his responsibilities to Nvidia's employees, board and shareholders.  He said: “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

His statement continued: "Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, Nvidia's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American."

Nvidia's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort".  It continued: "The Board prioritises US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders.

Alice Huang is linked to Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed.  Nvidia is a central player in AI infrastructure, providing chips to leading AI model developers including OpenAI and Meta. The microchip manufacturer is worth some $4.5 trillion, making it one of the most valuable companies ever.

China has previously rejected allegations of an espionage operation targeting Nvidia's chief, describing the claims as “groundless speculation”. 

However US intelligence agencies had been monitoring Alice Huang and concluded that she was acting on behalf of the Chinese government, according to unnamed sources cited by The New York Times. It remains unclear what information Alice Huang - who is also known as Huang Le - allegedly passed to Beijing, how valuable it was, or when she is believed to have begun gathering intelligence.

Reeta Chakrabarti presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Zoe Kleinman.

articles.title: Are There More Russell Brands In The Media Industry? | BBC News
articles.titleZh: 媒体行业中是否有更多罗素品牌？ | BBC新闻
articles.summary:
Today, we look at the political fallout from the Russell Brand case.

The Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy says there’s evidence that what happened with Russell Brand is still happening today and it’s time for the media industry to take abuse more seriously.

We also discuss calls for the rules be changed so victims in rape cases so women don’t feel like they are on trial, as some have said.

Subscribe to our channel here: https://bbc.in/bbcnews

For the latest news download the BBC News app or visit BBC.com/news

articles.title: Blanche: Dems should be ‘very worried’ after Trump ordered DOJ probe
articles.titleZh: 布兰奇：在特朗普下令司法部进行调查后，民主党人应该“非常担心”
articles.summary:
Attorney General Todd Blanche told CNN’s “State of the Union” today that members of the House Oversight Committee should be “very worried,” after President Donald Trump tasked the Department of Justice with investigating Democrats. 

It comes after Trump said Saturday he would have the DOJ look into threats of “Impeachment and many other forms of punishment” by Democrats against certain members of his administration, companies and donors to his ballroom project. 

Incoming House Oversight Committee Chair Rep. Robert Garcia (D-CA) and senior Oversight Committee member Rep. Stephen Lynch (D-MA) respond to Blanche's threat.

0:00 Attorney General Blanche comments on Trump's order to investigate Dems 
4:24 Will Blanche imprison Democrats? 
6:24 Blanche talks about representing Pete Hegseth if he's impeached 
9:16 Rep. Garcia responds to Blanche saying Dems should be worried 
10:44 Rep. Stephen Lynch says democracy is "a new thing" to Blanche 

Watch 24/7 live news with CNN Headlines: https://bit.ly/4eIvlTr

Stream more on CNN with an All Access subscription: https://cnn.it/4AZMu54

#Trump #Democrats #News
